facts.text: Sumiyoshi Taisha is the head shrine of 2,300 Sumiyoshi shrines nationwide and drew over 2 million pilgrims at New Year.
The shrine’s grounds feature four main halls designated national treasures, an arched bridge called Torihashi, and a sacred tree over 1,000 years old.
Sumiyoshi Taisha was erected before mainland Asia influenced Japanese architectural styles, making its third‑century design one of the oldest in Japan.
The ward’s southernmost part surrounds Sumiyoshi Grand Shrine, where long‑established local families have lived for centuries.
Suminoe Port, just south of the shrine, was Japan’s first international port and the departure point for envoys to China’s Sui and Tang dynasties.
In the Middle Ages, Emperor Go‑Murakami’s Southern Court stayed in the chief priest’s house at Sumiyoshi Grand Shrine for ten years, turning the area into a royal seat.
